text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is diagnosed when your blood pressure readings are consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg.

Blood pressure is measured using two numbers: systolic (the top number, measuring pressure when the heart beats) and diastolic (the bottom number, measuring pressure when the heart rests between beats).
According to guidelines from the American Heart Association and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, blood pressure is grouped into the following ranges:

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

list.snippet: Normal: Less than 120 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic
Elevated: 120–129 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic
Stage 1 Hypertension (High Blood Pressure): 130–139 mm Hg systolic or 80–89 mm Hg diastolic
Stage 2 Hypertension (High Blood Pressure): 140 mm Hg or higher systolic or 90 mm Hg or higher diastolic
Severe Hypertension / Hypertensive Crisis: Higher than 180 mm Hg systolic and/or higher than 120 mm Hg diastolic

Severe Hypertension (No Symptoms): If your reading is above 180/120 mm Hg but you feel fine, rest for a few minutes and recheck. If it remains that high, contact your healthcare professional immediately.

Hypertensive Emergency (With Symptoms): If your reading is above 180/120 mm Hg and you experience chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, weakness, a change in vision, or difficulty speaking, call 911 immediately.
